title: Effects of Sample Size and Geometry on Phase Transformation of Nanograined NiTi Micropillars
content: Shape memory alloys (SMAs) are a class of smart materials that have ability to “memorize” and restore their previous form or original shape after being subjected to thermomechanical stimuli from their environment. A non-diffusional martensitic phase transformation results in two unique properties, i.e., superelasticity and shape memory effect in SMAs [1]. SMAs have attracted much attention and interest in a broad range of applications [2]. These applications cover a wide span of length scales from meters down to nanometers. Hence, a crucial question about microstructure-macrostructure-function relation of SMAs has been raised, i.e., would an SMA sample of macro-, meso-, micro- and nanoscale sizes and different sample geometries behave differently [3–6]? This research was thus initiated to investigate the effects of sample size and geometry on phase transformation behavior of nanograined NiTi micropillars under compression.
